thread:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT: high kubelet restart rate detected for cluster:min-infer-west (nodes: gpu-west-4, gpu-west-6). Condition: kubelet_restart > 4/min for 3m. Possible impact: pod evictions and API 5xxs. Severity: P1. Page: maya_oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC24680

maya_oncall: acknowledged. Jumping in. Quick ask: error spike or timeouts?

lina_support: seeing spikes on /v1/chat and /v1/generate in west region. Error percent ~3.6%, some 502/503. A handful of accounts reported timeouts during heavy batch requests.

sam_infra: checking cluster: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=min-infer-west -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"Ready\")].status}{"\n"}{end}'` returns gpu-west-4 NotReady, gpu-west-6 NotReady, gpu-west-2 Ready.

ravi_sre: grabbed kubelet logs from gpu-west-6. Pattern shows repeated kubelet crashing with segfault and OOM messages. Also kernel log shows GPU driver reset events: `NVRM: Xid 116` followed by `oom_kill_process`. snippet:
```
Aug 22 11:03:12 kubelet[9876]: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
Aug 22 11:03:13 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:84:00): 116, GPU HANG
Aug 22 11:03:14 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 7890 (inference-worker)
```

leo_ml: container logs for inference-worker show `cuDNN: CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` and then the container restarts. Looks like heavy tensor batches triggered GPU driver fault.

maya_oncall: action plan: 1) quarantine flapping nodes (cordon + taint NoSchedule), 2) scale up pool by +3, 3) edge-route critical customer traffic to CPU fallback, 4) start collecting diagnostics and detaching these nodes from rotation. Any objections?

sam_infra: executing now. Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-west-4 && kubectl taint nodes gpu-west-4 node-role.kubernetes.io/quarantine=true:NoSchedule` then drain: `kubectl drain gpu-west-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`. Doing same for gpu-west-6. Also upping autoscaling desired to 18 from 15.

deploy-bot: No active rolling deploys for inference service. Last deploy 45m ago. No canaries.

ravi_sre: while draining, noticed several pods stuck in ContainerCreating complaining about device plugin init failure: `failed to allocate device: no devices available` — likely because device plugin crashed after driver reset.

leo_ml: recommend temporary routing rule for customer cohorts with IDs [2001, 4102] to `cpu-fallback-medium`. This avoids GPU initialization and should restore availability. I can push the route change if we agree.

maya_oncall: Lina, please send customer comms: brief & transparent. Sam, keep scaling and coordinate with infra to ensure new instances come with tested driver. Ravi, collect `/var/log/messages`, `journalctl -u kubelet -b -n 500`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `modinfo nvidia` and tar them. Use `incident-bundle` tool to upload.

lina_support: message sent: "We're investigating elevated errors in west region caused by node instability. We're routing traffic to backups and expect reduced errors in ~20 minutes. Will update." :mailbox_with_mail:

sam_infra: new nodes provisioning. Two new nodes joined: gpu-west-8, gpu-west-9. They report driver 495.46.83. Old nodes are running driver 495.29.05. Deciding whether to retire older driver nodes.

ravi_sre: collecting logs from gpu-west-6. `incident-bundle collect --node gpu-west-6 --out s3://redwood-incident/INC24680/gpu-west-6.tgz` uploaded. Kernel shows repeated `NVRM: Xid 116` events then system OOMs.

leo_ml: ruling out model code for now since multiple models triggered and issue correlates with older driver version + high sustained batch size. If we can't patch drivers immediately, plan B: evict pods from all nodes with driver 495.29.05 and keep them quarantined.

maya_oncall: agree. Sam, can you cordon nodes by driver version tag?

sam_infra: creating node selector based on label `nvidia-driver=495.29`. Running: `kubectl get nodes -l nvidia-driver=495.29 -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl cordon {}` then drain. Doing now.

leo_ml: in parallel I'll update the routing config to route customer IDs to CPU fallback. `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.local/routes -d '{"id": "inc24680-cpu-fallback","customer_ids": [2001,4102], "route": "cpu-fallback-medium"}'`

lina_support: customers updated with status and ETA 30m. No P0s yet but a few VIP accounts flagged for higher scrutiny.

sam_infra: drained two nodes and moved pods. New capacity absorbed the load; error rate down to 0.9% from 3.6%. Still watching.

maya_oncall: great. For remediation: Sam, open remediation ticket to retire nodes with driver 495.29 and coordinate a controlled driver upgrade to 495.46 on a small batch first. Ravi, attach diagnostic bundles and collect core dumps from kmod logs. Leo, reproduce on staging with same driver + stress test to try to trigger Xid116. Lina, prepare customer post-incident note draft.

sam_infra: ticket INFRA-4579 created. Adding runbook: rollback to previous driver or standardize on 495.46, add node gating to ensure driver matches cluster standard.

ravi_sre: started repro on staging. If we can reproduce GPU hang, we'll escalate to Nvidia with kernel logs. Also capturing `dmesg --ctime` and `systemd-coredump` entries to see if kubelet segfaults are from in-tree code or from container runtime.

leo_ml: quick note: consider rate-limiting very large batch requests at the gateway until driver situation is stable. This would reduce probability of driver memory leaks triggering.

maya_oncall: good suggestion. Can we add a temporary limit of batch_size <= 64 for west region via gateway policy?

deploy-bot: policy update applied: batch_size_max=64 for region=west for inference route.

lina_support: updated all affected customers: mitigation in place (nodes quarantined, CPU fallback for critical customers, scaling + batch limits). Next update in 1 hour or on any change.

incident-bot: INC24680 status: mitigated -> containment actions applied (node quarantine, autoscale, CPU fallback, gateway limits). Owner for postmortem: sam_infra. Slack thread will be closed for paging; keep this channel for follow-ups.

maya_oncall: handing off to Sam for full remediation and postmortem. I'll remain available for customer comms for 15m then hand to day-shift. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
